subject: Archaeology
title: Mohenjo-daro: City Without a Name
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mohenjo-daro: City Without a Name usable.

hook.text: In the 1920s, archaeologists in Pakistan found a 4,500-year-old city with indoor plumbing and grid streets.

buildup.text: Mohenjo-daro was part of the Indus Valley Civilization, which rivaled Egypt and Mesopotamia in scale.

discovery.text: The city had a Great Bath, standardized weights, and advanced drainage — but no palaces or temples.

twist.text: Nobody can read the Indus script. Without decoding it, we cannot know the city's real name or rulers.

climax.text: The city was abandoned around 1900 BCE. Climate change and river shifts likely made it unlivable.

punchline.text: A city with perfect plumbing left no readable words behind.

quiz.question: Why do we not know Mohenjo-daro's original name?
options: All records were destroyed in a fire
The Indus script has never been deciphered
The city predates the invention of writing
